assumptions: Admin access means role = admin only; support_lead, manager and staff lose admin endpoints.
Audited tables are tenants, refunds, users, customers and products: the tables edited or deleted by existing endpoints.
Admin API group is canonical 'admin'; admin/stats is under the admin path in the app group.
Removing role from me PATCH input is acceptable; callers sending it will be ignored.
audit_log.user_id is the acting user; for delete_user_account it is the deleted user (self-delete).
confusions: statement_required lists object kinds [query, tool, task, message] in the catalogue, but the recipe 'Record who changed what' puts deletes inside functions as the enforcement. The recipe does not say that the function's own deletes cannot be checked; I had to drop that rule.
Recipe's AUTH-002 build says 'tag admin' and 'paths'. The workspace admin group is an API group, so I used api_groups plus paths instead; the recipe does not say which to prefer when both exist.
Template AUTH-002 parameter examples show require_admin; the recipe uses require_role. I chose require_role to match the recipe.
Warning 'Function X is not on this branch' appears for objects created in the same change; it is expected but reads like an error when reviewing a dry run.

The skill says a rule can name an object kind of 'function' for statement rules; catalogue entry for object.statement_required does not list function, so the choice is not obvious from the skill alone.
wished_for: A check or statement rule that inspects deletes and writes inside called functions (or an explicit placement for functions in object.statement_required).
A check for change approval, or a documented way to represent an approval as a tag or table that a rule can read.
A recipe variant for SOC 2 CC6.x access reviews that says plainly it is not checkable, with a suggested non-policy evidence source.
An example of a precondition-based role check function in XanoScript to copy.
dry_run_problems_seen: Rule warning: AUTH-002.R1 api_groups only matches endpoints; fixed by adding object_kinds query.
Rule warnings: functions not on this branch for AUTH-002, AUDIT-EDITS, RET-001; expected because they are created in this change.
Dry run exited 0 with no blocked objects.
why_confidence: The policies check that edits to five tables call the audit function, that admin endpoints call a role check first, and that role cannot be written from input. None of that is evidence of change approval or access reviews, which the customer's auditor asks for. Deletes inside functions and creates are not audited. Admin-only is an assumption. Nothing is blocking, and the policies are advisory.
